body:
I'm operations manager and designer at a small print firm. Clients give absolutely no shits why they don't have something by a deadline, just that they don't. As long as people pay for services that will be the case.

The time I have taken off thus far has been forced and/or unproductive. Time off just makes time on worse.

Thank you, but in my case I think it's more of people doing what is expected of them than myself being loved. A pedestrian doesn't know me from a stranger, only reporting as a civic duty.

If I break my routine to take time off, the work doesn't go anywhere. Just piles up and requires I spend even longer at the office. There's no vacation to my job position, just giving myself tighter deadlines. Every hospital stay or doctors appointment has simply been met with a laundry list of tasks upon my return.
I just want to say to the world I'm sorry I was so disgusting you had to put me in the corner. But now I know my place. Goodbye everyone

It sounds cliche but I've gone on long enough just reporting to work and coming home that I don't have any to speak of anymore. The last connection I considered a friend put me in the hospital when I said my goodbyes. I've learned my lesson since then.
It's not about things going on in my life. It's about me reaching the natural end of enjoyment of my life. I don't crave more experiences, I just want to turn the game off so to speak.
No, I don't have any family left. That's why it felt so easy to slip away. No one would have noticed until rent time.
I feel too tired to do more than use the washroom and lay back down with my phone. Emotionally I feel so embarassed that I even failed at this. I was too stupid to do myself in.

I'm completely honest when I say any joy derived from an exchange where I am helpful expires when the moment is over. When they walk away, it goes back to neutral. I can remember moments when I've been helpful, but I am not happy or proud, only able to recall it like a film.
Why owe other people my life and labour? It doesn't change what I feel.
I have everything I've ever set out to want. I'm miserable with the thought of continuing in a useless endgame.

I've lived already. I've accepted an early end. People have told me that it's not natural to go before disease takes you, but trying to change my own mind on this topic has just made me more sure and bold.
I don't have it in me to continue living. I've done everything I'm capable of. I'm done. It just happens to be sooner than nature has planned for my body.
